document_update.purpose: Correct Sections 3.1 and 3.2 so that the Library is defined as a static, maximally complete, unbounded relational totality characterized by XOR closure and self-containment, rather than as a configuration space generated by a closure process. Preserve Closure_D(⊕) only as a mathematical characterization of closure, explicitly interpreted as a property rather than a temporal or ontological construction process.

authoritative_library_definition.definition: The maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying closure under XOR and self-containment with no definable privileged exterior. 𝓜 is a dimensionally undifferentiated complete relational totality, not a grid, container, temporal sequence, or singularity.

formal_characterization.self_containment: ¬∃z ∉ 𝓜 such that z is definable within the system using only ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D as a privileged exterior
formal_characterization.equivalence: 𝓜 is closed under XOR, self-contained with respect to its formal resources, and contains no privileged definable exterior

authoritative_library_definition.closure_interpretation: Closure_D(⊕) describes a closure property of 𝓜 and must not be interpreted as a temporal, generative, developmental, or ontological process by which 𝓜 comes into existence.
authoritative_library_definition.graph_interpretation: 𝓜 may be represented relationally as a complete graph in which configurations are mutually related without requiring intrinsic metric distance, spatial separation, or dimensional coordinates.

section_3.1.title_direction: Formal Domain and the Definition of the Library
section_3.1.primary_job: Establish the formal domain D and immediately distinguish the mathematical resources used to characterize 𝓜 from any claim that those resources temporally generate 𝓜.
required_order: Introduce D as the minimal formal domain required for ⊕ to have operands.
Define ⊕ as the primitive distinction operation.
Define 𝓜 by its global properties rather than by an operation that constructs it.
State XOR closure as a property of 𝓜.
State self-containment/no-definable-privileged-exterior as a property of 𝓜.
Explain that Closure_D(⊕) may be used as a mathematical characterization of the closure property.
Explicitly prohibit interpreting Closure_D(⊕) as temporal or ontological generation.
Establish that no generating configuration, generating set, coordinate, or construction history is privileged.
Establish that any admissible x ∈ 𝓜 may later serve as an observer-relative reference without becoming an ontological origin.

domain: D is a minimal formal domain containing configurations required for ⊕ to operate.
D is not physical space, spacetime, matter, energy, or an additional physical ontology.
primitive: ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
library_definition: 𝓜 is the maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying closure under XOR and self-containment with no definable privileged exterior.
No element outside 𝓜 is definable within the system as a privileged exterior using the formal resources of the system.
𝓜 is dimensionally undifferentiated: no intrinsic metric, spatial distance, coordinate grid, or temporal ordering is part of its foundational definition.
closure_statement: The notation Closure_D(⊕) may be retained as a mathematical shorthand for the fact that 𝓜 is closed under the primitive operation relative to the formal domain.
Closure_D(⊕) is a property-characterization, not a process.
The notation does not imply that D existed first in time and that 𝓜 was subsequently generated from D.
The notation does not identify any generating configuration as an ontological first state.
The notation does not establish a chronological history for the Library.
reference_neutrality: No x ∈ 𝓜 is privileged as an ontological origin or universal starting configuration.
Any x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as an observer-relative relational reference.
Changing the reference point changes the observer-relative relation over 𝓜, not the membership or structure of 𝓜 itself.

required_conceptual_correction.new_model: XOR as primitive distinction + D as formal substrate → 𝓜 defined as the unique maximally complete totality satisfying closure and self-containment
required_conceptual_correction.important_distinction: The formal domain supplies the language in which the Library's properties are expressed; it is not an ontological seed from which the Library develops.

generating_set_rule.statement: A generating set G may be used to algebraically address portions of 𝓜, but G is not an ontological origin of 𝓜.
generating_set_rule.interpretation: Generation language refers only to algebraic derivability or addressability within the formal structure. It must never be read as temporal creation.
generating_set_rule.prohibited_reading: G → 𝓜 as a cosmological development sequence.

termination_state.interpretation: 𝒵 is an internal termination/self-cancellation state of the XOR structure and is not an exterior, boundary, origin, or terminal region of 𝓜.
termination_state.important_rule: Reaching 𝒵 represents completion of distinction under the relevant operation, not escape from or deletion from the Library.

section_3.1.poetic_cipher: The Library is not built. It is the only room that contains every word the system can speak.
section_3.1.cipher_explanation: The metaphor is not intended to describe a physical container. The 'room' denotes the complete relational domain and the 'words' denote configurations expressible within the formal system. The Library is not assembled through time; it is characterized as the maximally complete totality in which the system's formal distinctions are already contained. No generating history is privileged.
section_3.1.handoff_to_3.2: Section 3.2 must therefore stop treating 𝓜 as an answer space produced by closure and instead describe the internal structure of the already-complete totality and the observer-relative relations induced over it.

section_3.2.title_direction: The Library as Complete Relational Totality
section_3.2.primary_job: Replace the residual answer-space interpretation with the static, dimensionally undifferentiated, maximally connected relational interpretation of 𝓜.

terminology.qualification_rule: The phrase 'answer space' may be retained only when explicitly referring to an observer-relative derived subset or continuation relation, never as a synonym for 𝓜 itself.

core_reframing.old_interpretation: 𝓜 is a large unbounded space containing candidate answers generated through XOR closure.
core_reframing.new_interpretation: 𝓜 is the static maximally complete relational totality. Observer-relative answer, accessibility, coherence, and continuation structures are relations induced over 𝓜.

structural_characterization.complete_relationality: The Library may be represented as a complete relational graph: every configuration is available as a relational operand with every other configuration without requiring intrinsic spatial distance.
structural_characterization.dimensionality: 𝓜 has no intrinsic dimensionality at the axiomatic floor.
structural_characterization.metric: No metric or distance function is primitive to 𝓜.
structural_characterization.adjacency: Adjacency is relational rather than spatial. There is no foundational notion of 'near' or 'far' inside 𝓜.
structural_characterization.separation: Any experienced separation between configurations is observer-relative and belongs to the derived relational structure, not to the ontology of 𝓜 itself.
structural_characterization.movement: Traversal is not spatial movement through a pre-existing metric space. It is the ordered maintenance or selection of coherent relations among configurations already contained in 𝓜.

maximality.definition: 𝓜 is maximally complete because no configuration, coordinate, worldline, or reference state is privileged as the universal origin of coherent traversal.
maximality.eternality: 𝓜 does not progress from simple to complex. It is unchanged under observer traversal: ∀i, 𝓜_i = 𝓜.
maximality.unboundedness: There is no privileged terminal region or excluded coordinate that determines where coherent traversal is permitted.
maximality.reference_neutrality: Any admissible x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as the observer's current relational reference without altering 𝓜.
maximality.observer_effect: Apparent temporal sequence, increasing complexity, locality, distance, and restriction of possible continuation arise from the observer's changing relation to 𝓜 rather than from changes to 𝓜.

observer_relation.whole_library_relation: The observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole 𝓜 at every abstract traversal step.
observer_relation.not_local_pre_filter: The observer does not first receive a locally bounded subset and then search inside it.
observer_relation.reference_point: The current x establishes the relational reference from which coherence and continuation are evaluated.
observer_relation.membership_separation: Observer-relative accessibility or coherence does not determine whether a configuration belongs to 𝓜.
observer_relation.non_erasure: x ∉ A_O does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.

coherent_continuation.principle: For every admissible observer-relative reference configuration x, the whole-Library relational evaluation must contain at least one coherent continuation above the observer's operative threshold under the model's stated assumptions.
coherent_continuation.formalization: ∀x ∈ 𝓜_admissible, ∀O with defined resolution floor I_N(O), ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜): γ begins at x ∧ 𝓒(γ|O,x) > γ_CO + ε, provided the observer's state admits continuation.
coherent_continuation.interpretation: The continuation is not generated after x. It is an observer-relative ordering among configurations already contained in the static totality.
coherent_continuation.causal_status: This nonempty continuation requirement is a derived structural requirement of the combined assumptions; it must not be presented as a theorem following from XOR closure alone.

no_singularity_clarification.reason: A singularity would collapse the structure to a distinguished point. 𝓜 instead denotes a maximally connected relational totality in which no point is privileged.
no_singularity_clarification.graph_analogy: A complete graph is a useful mathematical analogy because every vertex is relationally connected without requiring geometric distance. The analogy must not be interpreted as introducing graph topology as an additional physical axiom.

section_3.2.poetic_cipher: The Library is not the answers. It is the whole relation in which answers can become paths.
section_3.2.cipher_explanation: The Library contains configurations without classifying them as answers, futures, coherent states, or accessible states. Those classifications arise only through observer-relative relations over the totality. A path is therefore not a thing generated by the Library; it is a coherent ordering selected or maintained by the observer over configurations already contained within 𝓜.
section_3.2.handoff_to_4_1: Section 4.1 must inherit the distinction between the complete internal relational totality and any hypothetical external perspective. An external perspective cannot supply a privileged God's-eye ordering without introducing an additional relation not contained in the axiomatic floor.

cross_section_propagation.reason: Changing the semantic status of 𝓜 from generated closure to static maximal totality affects the interpretation of the formal domain, closure, observer accessibility, coherence, continuation, navigation, maximality, and the final dependency chain.
cross_section_propagation.global_semantic_rule: Every downstream subsection must treat 𝓜 as unchanged, static, maximally complete, and independent of observer accessibility or coherence. Observer-relative structures are relations over 𝓜, not mechanisms that construct or modify 𝓜.

revised_dependency_chain.critical_interpretive_rule: The arrow from D to 𝓜 denotes formal characterization/dependency, not temporal or ontological generation.
revised_dependency_chain.maximality_reason: Maximality is structurally required to prevent any configuration or worldline from becoming a privileged origin of coherent traversal.

global_language_replacements.replace: 𝓜 is the maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying XOR closure and self-containment; Closure_D(⊕) characterizes its closure property.

global_language_replacements.avoid: The Library is generated by XOR closure.
global_language_replacements.replace: The Library is characterized by XOR closure; closure is a property, not a generative process.
D provides the minimal formal domain in which the primitive operation and the Library's defining properties are expressed.

global_language_replacements.avoid: The Library is an answer space.
global_language_replacements.replace: The Library is the complete relational totality over which observer-relative answer and continuation relations are induced.

global_language_replacements.avoid: The Library contains all possible futures.
global_language_replacements.replace: The Library contains the complete static configuration totality; traversal establishes observer-relative ordered continuations within it.
The observer's relation to the unchanged Library changes.
The observer's experienced relational structure becomes more complex.

global_language_replacements.avoid: The Library is infinitely large in every direction.
global_language_replacements.replace: The Library is unbounded and dimensionally undifferentiated; it has no intrinsic directions or metric distance.
The observer traverses an ordered chain of coherent relations over 𝓜.
Every admissible observer-relative reference configuration admits at least one coherent continuation under the model's assumptions.

global_language_replacements.avoid: 𝒵 is the end of the Library.
global_language_replacements.replace: 𝒵 is an internal XOR termination/self-cancellation state within 𝓜.

editorial_invariants: 𝓜 is defined by property, not by temporal construction.
Closure_D(⊕) is a characterization of closure, not a process.
D is not an ontological seed or first state.
No generating set is an ontological origin.
𝓜 is static and eternally maximally complete.
𝓜 has no intrinsic dimensionality or metric.
𝓜 is not a physical container.
𝓜 is not an answer space.
𝓜 is not partitioned intrinsically into past and future.
Observer-relative structures are relations over 𝓜.
No configuration or worldline is privileged.
Arbitrary reference-point coherence is a derived requirement, not a consequence of XOR closure alone.
Continuation is relational traversal, not ontological generation.

3.1.cipher: The Library is not built. It is the only room that contains every word the system can speak.
3.1.explanation: The formal system does not narrate the construction of the Library through time. The Library is characterized as the maximally complete totality containing every configuration admitted by its defining relational structure. Closure describes the room's completeness, not the process of building it.

3.2.cipher: The Library is not the answers. It is the whole relation in which answers can become paths.
3.2.explanation: Configurations belong to the totality independently of whether an observer can resolve, access, or coherently traverse them. Paths, answers, accessibility, and experienced reality are observer-relative structures induced over the unchanged Library.

global.cipher: The whole was never becoming. It was already whole; only the relation changes.
global.explanation: The Library remains maximally complete at every abstract traversal step. Apparent succession, locality, distance, complexity, and temporal direction arise from the observer's changing relational reference, not from ontological development of 𝓜.
